title: Miami's Climate: Gridded History and Future CMIP6 Models Explained
description:
What does objective, model-driven data actually reveal about Miami's climate? In this video, we look past the headlines to examine the hard numbers of Miami's climate history and its conditional future outlook using precise coordinates (25.7620 N, -80.1920 W).

We break down the analysis into five clear sections:
1. Coordinates and Focus: Zooming in on Miami, Florida.
2. Reanalysis-Backed History (1981-2025): Looking at NASA POWER's MERRA-2 gridded data, which shows a baseline temperature increase of 1.06°C when comparing the first ten years of our dataset to the last ten. A least-squares trendline shows an average rise of 0.29°C per decade.
3. Future Projections (2040-2049): Evaluating the highly conditional SSP5-8.5 high-emissions scenario using three distinct CMIP6 models (ACCESS-CM2, MIROC6, and MPI-ESM1-2-HR). The models project a temperature increase ranging from 0.73°C to 1.59°C (median of 0.96°C) over their respective baselines.
4. Epistemic Limits: Understanding that gridded model cells (0.25-degree resolution) cannot fully resolve localized urban heat islands (like concrete or tree canopy) and do not project localized precipitation or storm-scale events in this subset.
5. Local Planning: Transitioning this data into actionable local planning questions for city zoning and infrastructure development.

Sources:
- NASA POWER Temporal API: https://power.larc.nasa.gov/docs/services/api/temporal/
- NASA POWER Methodology: https://power.larc.nasa.gov/docs/methodology/meteorology/
- NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 Details: https://www.nccs.nasa.gov/data-collections/nex-gddp-cmip6/
- NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 Registry: https://registry.opendata.aws/nex-gddp-cmip6/
